title: Make internal/testutil/headless take the browser from CHROME_BIN only (refusing Edge) and skip with a message naming CHROME_BIN otherwise

C8 (from WHAT): search the whole repository (scripts, docs, CI) for other places that pick a browser path, report them, fix the ones that are the same defect, and name the ones that are a different kind of change: missing
O-003 / m1 (the recorder's doc comment in default_browser_test.go still mentions Fatalf): a person waived it as note N-223, a comment-only fix left to the comment fixer, so I did not touch it.

Symlinks or hard links named chrome.exe that point at msedge.exe are not caught, because the check is by name and not by resolving links. That is not an ordinary-input spelling, so the corpus does not claim it. If it matters, resolving the target with filepath.EvalSymlinks in isEdge would close it.

drift: The accepted IN-M1 fix said to normalise with filepath.Abs, 'falling back to filepath.Clean if that fails'. isEdge (headless.go:83-91) has no Clean fallback: when Abs errors it returns false, so only the raw-text check applies. The build did not declare this. I found no consequence. On Windows, Abs errors only on strings GetFullPathName rejects, which os.Stat cannot open either, so Browser skips. On Unix, `msedge.exe/.` does not resolve to the file at all.

Nothing asked which spellings of a path resolve to that file: `msedge.exe\.`, `\.\.`, `\x\..`, `/.`, `msedge.exe \.`, a trailing dot or space. The first build checked only filepath.Base of the raw CHROME_BIN text, so Edge got past the refusal and exec.Command would have started it. The critique did not run because the slice was sized medium risk with 0 designers. A check that could have been written: set CHROME_BIN to <tmp>\msedge.exe plus each of those suffixes and assert a skip naming CHROME_BIN.

caused_by.reason: 1 obligation(s) landed on this stage after it passed (O-002), so nothing downstream was ever going to carry them out and the merge would have refused. Sent back with what raised them: O-002 (fix): IN-M1 (major): isEdge only checks the last text element of CHROME_BIN. On Windows, a path ending in a '.' or 'x\..' segment names msedge.exe itself, so Edge gets past the refusal. Measured on this machine with an empty dummy file <tmp>\msedge.exe: Browser returned the path without skipping for CHROME_BIN=<tmp>\msedge.exe\., \.\., \x\.., /. and 'msedge.exe \.'. os.Stat resolves each of these to msedge.exe, a regular file. exec.Command runs the file such a path resolves to: `C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe\.` and `cmd.exe\x\..` both ran cmd.exe and printed the echo. So CHROME_BIN=C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe\. makes Shot start Edge. That breaks criterion 5 and the design's case that a file whose base name is msedge.exe must be skipped. In isEdge, resolve the path the way the OS will before taking its base name: `if a, err := filepath.Abs(p); err == nil { p = a }`, then `base := strings.ToLower(filepath.Base(p))`. On Windows, filepath.Abs calls GetFullPathName, the same normalisation CreateFile and CreateProcess apply. Keep returning the CHROME_BIN text unchanged. With this change in an overlay, the repro and the whole package pass. CLOSE THE CLASS, NOT THIS INSTANCE. IN-M1 is one member of "path spellings whose last text element is not the file the OS opens" (members come from ordinary input, by accident). Enumerate the class into a corpus committed with the code -- a table of inputs, fire/quiet plant rows, an alias list, a census of every type that carries the value -- in the repository or .taad/slices/SL-014/, make every row pass, and show the code before your fix failing the rows you claim to close. Bound the class by who produces its members, not by every exotic spelling. Answer this obligation with `corpus`: the corpus's path from the repository root. It is not discharged without one. [shown by a failing run] The engine ran the code review's test for this, internal/testutil/headless/edge_dot_segments_test.go, with `go test -count=1 -run TestBrowserRefusesEdgeBehindDotSegments ./internal/testutil/headless/`, and it FAILED. Put that test at internal/testutil/headless/edge_dot_segments_test.go as it is -- comments and layout aside -- and make it pass. The engine runs `go test -count=1 -run TestBrowserRefusesEdgeBehindDotSegments ./internal/testutil/headless/` again in your tree, and that run is what closes this; your word does not. The test: package headless import ( "fmt" "os" "path/filepath" "runtime" "strings" "testing" ) // dotRecorder stands in for the calling test so the skip can be observed. type dotRecorder struct { testing.TB skipped bool msg string } func (r *dotRecorder) Skip(args ...any) { r.skipped = true; r.msg = fmt.Sprint(args...) } func (r *dotRecorder) Skipf(format string, args ...any) { r.skipped = true r.msg = fmt.Sprintf(format, args...) } func (r *dotRecorder) SkipNow() { r.skipped = true } // Windows resolves "." and ".." in a path by its text, so C:\...\msedge.exe\. // names msedge.exe itself: os.Stat finds it and exec starts it. Browser must // refuse it as Edge, as it refuses ...\msedge.exe. Nothing is started here. func TestBrowserRefusesEdgeBehindDotSegments(t *testing.T) { if runtime.GOOS != "windows" { t.Skip("only Windows resolves msedge.exe\\. to the file itself") } edge := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "msedge.exe") if err := os.WriteFile(edge, nil, 0o644); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) } shapes := map[string]string{ "trailing dot": edge + `\.`, "two trailing dots": edge + `\.\.`, "up and back": edge + `\x\..`, "slash dot": edge + `/.`, "space before slash": edge + ` \.`, } for name, p := range shapes { t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) { t.Setenv("CHROME_BIN", p) r := &dotRecorder{TB: t} got := Browser(r) if !r.skipped || got != "" { t.Fatalf("CHROME_BIN=%q names msedge.exe, yet Browser returned %q without skipping", p, got) } if !strings.Contains(r.msg, "CHROME_BIN") { t.Fatalf("the skip message does not name CHROME_BIN: %q", r.msg) } }) } }
